title: GPUParticles3D: AT_COLLISION sub-emitter events are dropped unless fixed_fps is set to 30
body:
### Tested versions

4.6.2.stable.official (Windows 11, Forward+, D3D12)




### System information

Godot v4.6.2.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 3 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9597) - AMD Ryzen 9 7900 12-Core Processor (24 threads) - 47.21 GiB memory

### Issue description

A GPUParticles3D node with collision_mode = HIDE_ON_CONTACT and sub_emitter_mode = AT_COLLISION silently drops a significant fraction of collision events.

The reliability of sub-emitter firing depends heavily on the parent's fixed_fps setting. Only fixed_fps = 30 reliably fires the sub-emitter for every collision. Any other value—including the default 0 (render FPS)—results in missed events.

Furthermore, the bug is exacerbated by engine performance; if the editor loses focus and the FPS drops, even fixed_fps = 30 begins to fail. This suggests a race condition or buffer synchronization issue between the GPU particle simulation steps and the event consumer.

Expected behavior:
Every parent particle collision should trigger the sub-emitter exactly once, independent of the fixed_fps setting or the current application frame rate.

### Steps to reproduce

Create a GPUParticles3D node emitting particles downwards.

Add a GPUParticlesCollisionBox3D as a ground collider.

Set the particles' collision_mode to HIDE_ON_CONTACT.

Assign a sub-emitter with sub_emitter_mode set to AT_COLLISION.

Run the project with fixed_fps = 60 (or the default 0). Notice some particles disappear upon hitting the collider without spawning the sub-emitter.

Change fixed_fps = 30 and notice it works correctly while the window is focused.

Defocus the window (reducing FPS) and observe the collisions failing again even at fixed_fps = 30.

| Rain.fixed_fps | Focused (High FPS) | Unfocused (Low FPS) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 (default) | Misses events | Many misses |
| 30 | **No misses** | Misses events |
| 60 | Misses events | Many misses |
| 120 | More misses | Many misses |


**Note: This issue is not limited to the editor viewport; it also occurs in the actual game instance when running the project (F5).**

Note on Hardware: I have confirmed that this issue is also reproducible on a secondary PC with an NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050, indicating this is not hardware-specific to high-end GPUs.
